newsitem.title: UK: Burmah eases after in-line first half.
newsitem.headline: Burmah eases after in-line first half.

text.p: Shares in Burmah Castrol Plc slipped in pre-market trading on Monday after first-half results broadly met market expectations, analysts said.
Net income rose 13 percent to 67.7 million stg against analyst forecasts ranging from 60.2 to 70.0 million stg.
The dividend was raised nine percent to 12 pence per share.
By 0717 GMT Burmah shares had eased 7-1/2p to 1042-1/2p.

"There were maybe a couple of areas that were just a bit weaker than expected. There weren't any positive surprises but I wouldn't be particularly surprised to see the shares finish the day higher," said one trader.
A slightly lower than-expected dividend was cited as one reason for the early share price weakeness.

Burmah chief executive Jonathan Fry said Europe had been significantly affected by the poor conditions in Germany while markets remained competitive in the U.S. Asia was buoyant across the whole region.

"The results are quite pleasing against a difficult European trading environment. They benefited from lower interest charges because of the cash received from the sale of Fuels' operations and that helped gearing come down as well," said SG Strauss Turnbull analyst Irene Himona.

The Fuels disposal programme continued with the sale of operations in Chile, Sweden and Turkey realising some 90 million stg. The results included an exceptional profit of 23 million stg from disposals in the Fuels portfolio.

Market conditions are not expected to change significantly from the first half. North American markets have yet to show signs of improvement, Germany may be past its low point and Asia'a growth momentum is continuing, the company said.
"Overall it was a pleasing performance. The prospective ratings are below market average and it's one of the cheapest stocks in the sector and advise buying the shares," said Himona.

While chemical margins were slightly below expectation, said Chartehouse Tilney analyst Chris Perry, the company had stated an intention to achieve margins of around 10 percent, leaving scope for improvement.
Elsewhere in the sector continuing tensions in Iraq helped keep other oil stocks firm in early trading.

U.N. secretary general Boutros Boutros Ghali said on Sunday he would delay the oil-for-food plan until he could assess the situation in northern Iraq. Traders said the oil market would watch closely any U.N. response to Iraq's decision on Sunday to withdraw troops from northern kurdish areas.
Shares in British Petroleum rose 4-1/2p to 627p, Shell Transport & Trading 7p to 939-1/2p, Lasmo was up 4-1/2p at 198p and Enterprise Oil 9p at 518-1/2p.
